title: How Rotterdam is reinventing religious heritage for city life
content:
Rotterdam has spent much of its modern history reinventing itself. Rebuilt after the devastation of the Second World War, the city became a testing ground for new ideas in architecture, planning and urban development. The spirit of reconstruction remains deeply embedded in Rotterdam’s identity, shaping a city where innovation and adaptation are part of everyday life.

This legacy has also shaped Rotterdam’s relationship with its own past. With much of its historic urban fabric destroyed in 1940, the city cannot draw on an extensive stock of pre-war monuments to sustain a sense of continuity with history. Instead, its connection to heritage has become an inherently intangible one, carried through personal stories, memory and community narratives as much as through buildings themselves. This human-centred approach appears to have infused the way Rotterdam engages with culture and heritage more broadly. Combined with its identity as a port city with a long history of migration and cultural diversity, it creates a distinctive context, one that sets Rotterdam apart from cities that can rely on an imposing stock of built heritage as a source of attractiveness and local pride.

title: Hub releases second “In Varietate Concordia” Podcast episode featuring Sabine Verheyen
content:
Following the inaugural episode with Portuguese pianist Maria João Pires, the In Varietate Concordia Podcast presents a conversation between Sabine Verheyen, First Vice-President of the European Parliament, and Sneška Quaedvlieg-Mihailović,  Secretary General of Europa Nostra and Project Leader of the European Heritage Hub. They discuss the political and economic value of culture, the history and layers of the European identity, and what Europe needs to do for the cultural sector. 

Together, they “travel” to the city of Aachen, where Ms. Verheyen spent her childhood and began her political career, and trace the threads that led her to become one of the most fervent advocates for culture and cultural heritage in the European political landscape.

title: Join the Hub’s deep-dive webinar on inclusive heritage case studies from Rotterdam, Umbria and Antwerp
content:
On 18 September, join the European Heritage Hub for the webinar “Sharing Local Stories: Cultural Heritage for Inclusive Cities and Regions”. 

During this session, we will dive into the key lessons from our recent Peer-Learning Visit to Rotterdam from 18-20 June, and discover connected initiatives in other European cities and regions! You will get insights into the content of the visit, including recommendations for cities, regions and cultural heritage stakeholders, from the expert who facilitated the Peer-Learning programme. You will also learn about two case studies from the participating cultural heritage practitioners.

  • Tanja Mlaker, Director Cultuur Eindhoven (The Netherlands) – Hub Peer-Learning Visit expert
  • Martijn van der Mark, City of Rotterdam (The Netherlands) – Hub Peer-Learning Visit host
  • Greet Donckers, Cultural Heritage Consultant, City of Antwerp (Belgium)
  • Gianluigi Bettin, Project Manager, Sviluppumbria – Regional agency of economic development in Umbria (Italy)
